title: Chemical Changes
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Chemical Changes Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: Reactivity of metals: metal oxides, the reactivity series, extraction of metals and reduction, oxidation and reduction in terms of electrons; reactions of acids with metals, neutralisation of acids and salt production, soluble salts, the pH scale and neutralisation, strong and weak acids; electrolysis of molten ionic compounds and aqueous solutions, and the extraction of metals using electrolysis.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on chemical changes: the reactivity series, extraction and reduction, acids and salts, pH and neutralisation, strong and weak acids, and electrolysis. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Metals form at the cathode; non-metals at the anode.
body_html:
How to think about it

Metals react according to the reactivity series.

  • Metals below carbon are extracted by reduction with carbon; reactive metals by electrolysis.
  • acid + metal → salt + hydrogen; acid + base → salt + water; acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.
  • In electrolysis, positive ions go to the cathode and negative ions go to the anode.
Example

Copper oxide + sulfuric acid?

base + acid

Answer: copper sulfate + water

Example

Electrolysis of brine: cathode?

Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen

Answer: hydrogen

Common mistakes

  • Thinking acid + carbonate gives hydrogen.
  • Thinking strong means concentrated.
  • Thinking brine electrolysis gives sodium.

faq.q: How do you name a salt?
faq.a: Use the metal's name, then the acid part: hydrochloric acid makes chlorides, sulfuric acid sulfates and nitric acid nitrates.
An electric current passes through a molten or dissolved ionic compound. Positive ions move to the cathode and gain electrons; negative ions move to the anode and lose electrons.

faq.q: What is the difference between strong and weak acids?
faq.a: Strong acids such as hydrochloric acid ionise completely in water. Weak acids such as ethanoic acid only partly ionise.
